insights: HurwitzQuat stored as (n0,n1,n2,n3)/2 with equal-parity condition; parity ensures normSq4 divisible by 4
omega = half(1+i+j+k) is a Hurwitz unit (N=1) - its inclusion makes H Euclidean
Rotation trick (n0±n1)/2 gives 2p not p for half-integer case - cannot convert directly
Norm multiplicativity follows directly from Mathlib Quaternion.normSq_mul via toQuat embedding

Hurwitz's 1896 addition of ω = (1+i+j+k)/2 to the Lipschitz ring drops the covering radius of the quaternion lattice from exactly 1 (D4 root lattice) to √2/2 (D4* weight lattice) — exactly the geometric statement that makes left-Euclidean division work and gives the four-square representation for free.

The four-square identity (a²+b²+c²+d²)(e²+f²+g²+h²) = A²+B²+C²+D² used in Lagrange's 1770 descent proof IS quaternion norm multiplicativity N(qr) = N(q)·N(r); the descent proof and the Hurwitz proof share their multiplicative core, differing only in how the prime case is handled (combinatorial descent vs. structural Euclidean factorization).

Mathlib's `EuclideanDomain` typeclass assumes commutativity (via `CommRing`), so a direct `EuclideanDomain HurwitzInt` instance is blocked. The workaround at original ship was to axiomatize the division-with-remainder property and use it directly; discharging the axiom requires building a non-commutative left-Euclidean framework or proving covering-radius geometrically.
